# Calibrated Interpretation: Confidence Estimation in Semantic Parsing

## Research question

A parser may assign confidence that poorly reflects whether its complete executable program matches the user’s request, and measured calibration depends on how correctness is labeled.

## Method

The study uses maximum token probabilities, minimum aggregation over subwords and generated programs, adaptive calibration bins and reliability plots. It compares fine-tuned parsers and a separate few-shot CodeGen setting rather than learning a new post-hoc calibration map.

## Evaluation

English Spider/CoSQL use BenchCLAMP splits and fine-tuned T5, BART and Code-T5; dialogue datasets supply additional comparisons. Token diagnostics use gold-prefix teacher forcing, while sequence confidence uses generated prefixes. Exact match is the main label, with a separate T5-base Spider test-suite execution analysis and a three-seed difficulty study.

## What the results support

SQL token predictions are more overconfident than those of the same architectures on the tested dialogue datasets. Test-suite labels reduce apparent overconfidence relative to strict SQL exact match. Higher Spider input perplexity and harder programs are associated with calibration problems; the released confidence-selected challenge splits concern dialogue parsing only.

## Limits and qualifications

Teacher-forced token calibration is not free-running sequence reliability. Exact match penalizes valid alternatives, and finite execution suites are not semantic proofs. Perplexity is an OOD proxy; correlations do not establish a distribution-shift guarantee. English datasets, historical models, binning choices and model-selected challenge subsets constrain generalization; no live clarification or abstention outcome is measured.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Provides a useful calibration-measurement baseline and reusable metric library for SQL confidence studies, while showing why confidence must be interpreted together with the evaluator and generation protocol.
